name: Encircling Double Aortic Arch

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Imaging Diagnostic Criteria for Double Aortic Arch

criteria.description: Identification of two aortic arches forming a complete vascular ring encircling the trachea and esophagus on imaging
Presence of respiratory symptoms attributable to tracheal compression such as stridor or wheezing
Symptoms of esophageal compression including dysphagia or feeding difficulties

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of imaging-confirmed double aortic arch forming a vascular ring plus at least one major clinical symptom of airway or esophageal compression
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily based on imaging modalities such as echocardiography, CT angiography, or MRI combined with clinical presentation.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Inspiratory stridor due to tracheal compression
searchTerms: noisy breathing when inhaling due to trachea pressure
trouble swallowing due to food pipe blockage

pathognomonic.symptomName: Biphasic wheezing associated with vascular ring
searchTerms: wheezing with two phases linked to vascular ring
biphasic wheeze from blood vessel anomaly

common.symptomName: Stridor exacerbated by crying or feeding
searchTerms: stridor worsens with crying or feeding
noisy breathing increases during feeding or crying
temporary stops in breathing at night

occasional.symptomName: Failure to thrive due to feeding impairment
searchTerms: poor growth due to feeding difficulties
failure to gain weight from eating problems

occasional.symptomName: Hoarseness from recurrent laryngeal nerve irritation
searchTerms: voice changes due to recurrent laryngeal nerve
chest wall pulling in during breathing
visible chest muscle sinking with breaths
noisy breathing worsening to breathing difficulty
coughing up blood from airway damage
blood in sputum due to airway erosion

rare.symptomName: Pulmonary hypertension secondary to chronic airway obstruction
searchTerms: high blood pressure in lungs from airway blockage
lung artery pressure increase due to airway disease
pulmonary artery hypertension from breathing obstruction

imaging: Echocardiography showing two aortic arches forming a vascular ring
CT angiography or MRI demonstrating complete encirclement of trachea and esophagus by double aortic arch
other: Clinical presentation of stridor and feeding difficulties in infancy
Response to surgical division of the smaller aortic arch

distinguishingFeatures: Single aortic arch with aberrant vessel rather than complete vascular ring
Anomalous origin of left pulmonary artery causing airway compression
Different surgical approach and imaging findings

redFlags: Failure to thrive due to feeding impairment
